answers.answer: Drowning destroys Towns/Cities, so their Fear occurs immediately and drowned Invaders go on Ocean’s panel. In a two-Spirit game, the exchange rate is 2 printed Health worth for 1 Energy; a City is worth 3 printed Health and can supply one Energy exchange with change. evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. answers.answer: Separate Power uses cannot combine Bringer’s hypothetical Damage; 2 plus 1 in separate Powers does not destroy the City. Instructions within one Power can combine, and a Repeat can pretend-destroy the same piece again.

evidence.text:
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally. Apply these results separately to each would-be-destroyed Invader; the Fear result does not itself grant movement:

  | Would-be-destroyed Invader | Fear | Movement from this special rule |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Explorer | 0 | Push it. |
  | Town | 2 | Push it. |
  | City | 5 | No Push. |

  No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]

answers.answer: If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus and is thereby destroyed, it is destroyed in its destination land, never in an in-between location.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. requested_parts: ordinary Repeat phase after Fast then made Slow
answers.answer: An ordinary Repeat uses the Power’s most recently assigned speed, so it repeats in Slow after being made Slow. An explicit instruction to Repeat immediately follows its stated timing.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.
